title: Atmosphere view: dome + skybox crossfade wiring (the no-pop visual transition)
description: TASK-28 is ~55% committed and green: the shared boundary math (spec step 1), per-planet density, the inverted drag ramp, all shared/sim tests, the fixed TASK-25 flight test, and the atmosphere-dome module (src/client/render/atmosphere-dome.ts) are all DONE and committed. What remains for the visual-transition acceptance criterion ('skybox crossfades to an atmosphere dome as the player descends through the boundary band — a continuous blend, no pop at any altitude') is to WIRE the dome into the live view: (a) a pure per-planet 'atmosphere view' helper that, for a position, resolves the owning planet + its boundary + haze, and (b) the WorldManager owning the dome mesh and fading the skybox/starfield with the SAME haze number (the spec's no-desync contract: both driven by one number). This task delivers that live wiring + its unit tests. It does NOT touch the re-entry tint (TASK-28.2) or the e2e pixel probe (TASK-28.3).

steps.description: Pure atmosphere-view helper — NEW src/client/world/atmosphere-view.ts (~60 lines)
steps.details: Imports: regimeFor + type Regime from '@shared/regime'; systemRegimePlanets, planetAtmosphereRadius, planetAtmosphereDensity from '@shared/galaxy/planets'; boundaryFactor, hazeFactor from '@shared/physics/atmosphere'; type Planet, SystemGen from '@shared/galaxy/types'; type Vec3 from '@shared/physics/vec'. Export `interface AtmosphereView { planet: Planet | null; altitude: number; boundary: number; haze: number }`. Export `function atmosphereViewFor(pos: Vec3, system: SystemGen | null, current: Regime = 'space'): AtmosphereView`: if `system === null` -> space result `{ planet: null, altitude: pos.y, boundary: 0, haze: 0 }`; else `const result = regimeFor(pos, systemRegimePlanets(system), current, 0)`; if `result.regime === 'space'` -> the same space result; else `planet = system.planets.find((p) => p.id === result.planetId)` (non-null by construction), `altitude = pos.y` (flat client terrain; anchors sit at y=0), `boundary = boundaryFactor(altitude, planet)`, `haze = hazeFactor(altitude, { atmosphereRadius: planetAtmosphereRadius(planet), atmosphereDensity: planetAtmosphereDensity(planet) })`. CRITICAL: the caller passes the LIVE regime as `current` so the exit hysteresis band [1000,1050) stays consistent with the sim (the band is 'space' or 'atmosphere' depending on history). Unit test `src/client/world/atmosphere-view.test.ts` (fixture-system pattern from app/src/client/state/regime-wiring.test.ts — derive one system from generateStars(SEED, N)[0].id then generateSystem): assert (a) mid-band altitude (pos = anchor + (0, 500, 0)) gives boundary ≈ 0.5 and haze = 0.5 × densityScale(planetAtmosphereDensity(planet)) computed from the SAME shared functions; (b) a far/space position gives planet null + boundary 0 + haze 0; (c) a position in the exit band [1000,1050) with current='atmosphere' keeps the planet (boundary still > 0) but the SAME position with current='space' yields null; (d) an airless planet gives space/null/0. Verify with `cd app && npx vitest run src/client/world/atmosphere-view.test.ts`.

steps.description: WorldManager: own the dome + crossfade the skybox with one haze number (src/client/world/WorldManager.ts, +~40 lines)
steps.details: Add imports: createAtmosphereDome, ATMOSPHERE_HAZE_COLORS, type AtmosphereDome from '@client/render/atmosphere-dome'; planetAnchor from '@shared/galaxy/planets'; ATMOSPHERE_BOUNDARY_M from '@shared/physics/atmosphere'; type Regime from '@shared/regime'; type Vec3 from '@shared/physics/vec'; atmosphereViewFor from './atmosphere-view'. New fields: `private system: SystemGen | null = null;` (store the OBJECT — currentSystemId stays a string for the existing contract), `private readonly dome: AtmosphereDome;`, `private readonly tempColor = new THREE.Color();`. In the constructor AFTER `this.background = createBackground(seed)`: set `(this.background.sky.material as THREE.MeshBasicMaterial).transparent = true;` (sky opacity starts at 1; the stars material is ALREADY transparent @ 0.95 from createBackground — do not touch its base), then `this.dome = createAtmosphereDome(ATMOSPHERE_BOUNDARY_M);` (every atmospheric planet shares ATMOSPHERE_BOUNDARY_M per planetAtmosphereRadius, so ONE dome serves all — spec: 'at most one dome is active at a time') and `this.scene.add(this.dome.mesh);`. In `swapWorld(system)`: also set `this.system = system;`. New method — ONE number drives dome AND skybox (the no-desync contract): `setAtmosphereView(pos: Vec3, current: Regime = 'space'): void { const view = atmosphereViewFor(pos, this.system, current); if (view.planet) { const anchor = planetAnchor(this.system!.planets.indexOf(view.planet)); this.dome.mesh.position.set(anchor.x, 0, anchor.z); this.dome.set(view.haze, this.tempColor.setFromHex01(ATMOSPHERE_HAZE_COLORS[view.planet.class])); } else { this.dome.set(0, this.tempColor); } const fade = 1 - view.haze; (this.background.sky.material as THREE.MeshBasicMaterial).opacity = fade; (this.background.stars.material as THREE.PointsMaterial).opacity = 0.95 * fade; }`. `setFromHex01` is a tiny THREE.Color helper (add it inline or as a module fn): parse `#rrggbb` and call `setRGB(r/255, g/255, b/255, THREE.NoColorSpace)` — MUST use NoColorSpace (raw sRGB floats; see dead ends). In `dispose()`: add `this.dome.dispose();`. Note: world-manager.test.ts tests ONLY the pure `buildSystemLayout` — the WebGL path is exercised by tsc + the e2e in TASK-28.3; do NOT try to unit-test the WebGL path here.

steps.description: Wire the live path into the session (src/client/main.tsx) + full verify + commit
steps.details: The self entity_update handler lives in the useGameSession hook (main.tsx line ~116-129); the WorldManager lives in App (worldRef, line ~338). They are DIFFERENT scopes — you CANNOT call worldRef.current?.setAtmosphereView(...) directly inside the handler, and passing worldRef as a direct argument to the hook would hit the temporal-dead-zone (it is declared at line ~338, AFTER the hook call at line ~272, and would be read during render). Bridge with a CALLBACK PARAM: (a) give useGameSession an optional param `onAtmosphereView?: (pos: Vec3, regime: Regime) => void`; in the handler, right after `if (self) regimeWiring.onSelfUpdate(self, Date.now());`, add `if (self) onAtmosphereView?.(self.pos, regimeWiring.regime);` (the hook owns regimeWiring, so it passes the live regime — keeps the exit hysteresis consistent). (b) In App, the `useGameSession(...)` call (line ~272) passes `onAtmosphereView: (pos, regime) => { worldRef.current?.setAtmosphereView(pos, regime); }` — a CLOSURE that reads worldRef.current only when invoked (on WS messages, post-mount), so it is TDZ-safe. Add Regime/Vec3 type imports to main.tsx as needed. Verify: `cd app && npx vitest run src/client/world/atmosphere-view.test.ts` (new), then `cd app && npx vitest run` (full ~740 tests green), `cd app && npm run typecheck`, `cd app && npm run lint`. Kill any background dev server, then commit (Conventional Commit, e.g. `feat(TASK-28.1): atmosphere view — dome + skybox crossfade wiring (one-number, no-desync blend)`) and STOP.

acceptanceCriteria: atmosphereViewFor (new, pure, src/client/world/atmosphere-view.ts) returns: boundary ≈ 0.5 and haze = 0.5 · densityScale(planetAtmosphereDensity) at a mid-band altitude for an atmospheric planet; planet null + boundary 0 + haze 0 in space; the exit hysteresis band [1000,1050) respects the passed `current` regime (current='atmosphere' keeps the planet, current='space' yields null); an airless planet yields space/null/0 — all asserted in a deterministic unit test

ONE number (view.haze) drives both the dome (dome.set(view.haze, ...)) and the skybox fade (sky.opacity = 1 - view.haze and stars.opacity = 0.95 · (1 - view.haze)) — so the two can never desync; the dome is hidden (zero cost, mesh.visible false) when haze ≤ 1e-4 and is positioned at the owning planet's surface anchor
The live path is wired: every self entity_update calls setAtmosphereView(self.pos, <live tracker regime>) via the useGameSession callback param
cd app && npx vitest run: full unit suite green; cd app && npm run typecheck clean; cd app && npm run lint clean; committed and the working tree is clean
notes: PICKS UP WHERE TASK-28 STOPPED. TASK-28 failed twice by RUNNING OUT OF TIME — this is a sizing problem, NOT an environment problem (vitest is ~85 s; headless-WebGL Playwright is already proven green by TASK-26.2 and TASK-27). No exploration is needed: the design below is fixed and every reference file was read and confirmed.

ALREADY COMMITTED & GREEN (commit 44202f3 — do NOT re-do): src/shared/physics/atmosphere.ts (boundaryFactor, densityScale, hazeFactor, reentryTintFactor + constants ATMOSPHERE_BOUNDARY_M=1000, ATMOSPHERE_REF_DENSITY=0.1, REENTRY_TINT_SPEED=200, REENTRY_TINT_RAMP=300, REENTRY_TINT_MAX=0.4); src/shared/physics/flight.ts (drag calls boundaryFactor; PlanetAtmo has atmosphereRadius; integrateStep takes the planet); src/shared/galaxy/planets.ts (planetAtmosphereDensity = class base [rocky 0.04/ice 0.05/terran 0.08/ocean 0.1/gas 0.12] × seeded [0.5,1.0) via hash2(seedFromString(id), 0x57413417n); planetAtmosphereRadius = hasAtmosphere ? 1000 : 0; systemRegimePlanets); src/server/shard/shard.ts (per-planet density+radius in the flight context; ATMO_DENSITY constant removed); ALL shared/sim tests; the fixed src/server/shard/shard.regime.test.ts (TASK-25); and src/client/render/atmosphere-dome.ts (the back-face dome: createAtmosphereDome(radiusU), ATMOSPHERE_HAZE_COLORS per planet class, DOME_SKY_COLOR, set(haze, atmoColor, skyColor?) that copies color components VERBATIM into the Vector3 uniforms, mesh hidden when haze ≤ 1e-4, radius = radiusU × 1.01) + its 5-test file.

WORKING TREE is CLEAN: all code is in commit 44202f3; the only uncommitted change in HEAD (3513eb2) is the handoff rewrite (.ralph/handoff/TASK-28.md). Baseline at handoff: `cd app && npx vitest run` ~741 pass / 1 skip; `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; lint clean. Verified directly against the code: atmosphere.ts, planets.ts, atmosphere-dome.ts, WorldManager.ts, regime-wiring.ts, main.tsx all match the handoff; WorldManager/regime-wiring/main.tsx do NOT yet have the wiring this task adds (confirmed absent).

WIRING GAP the handoff got subtly wrong: the handoff's inline `worldRef.current?.setAtmosphereView(...)` inside the entity_update handler is NOT possible as written — regimeWiring + the handler live in the useGameSession hook (main.tsx ~104/116) while worldRef lives in App (~338, declared AFTER the hook call at ~272). Use the callback-param bridge in step 3; do NOT pass worldRef itself as a direct hook argument (TDZ).

DEAD ENDS (do not repeat): (a) three.js ColorManagement — feed the dome RAW 0..1 sRGB floats (`setRGB(r/255,g/255,b/255, THREE.NoColorSpace)` or set the uniform Vector3s directly); `new THREE.Color(hex)` converts sRGB→linear working space but the raw ShaderMaterial writes gl_FragColor with NO output transform, so it renders too dark and breaks the e2e pixel math (TASK-28.3). (b) preserveDrawingBuffer: true is required to readPixels outside the rAF loop (headless SwiftShader) — it is already on the WorldManager/renderer; keep it on any probe renderer. (c) The regime hysteresis means the [1000,1050) band can resolve to 'space' OR 'atmosphere' by history — that is why atmosphereViewFor takes `current: Regime`; always pass the LIVE tracker regime. (d) A single velocity impulse can NEVER escape the atmosphere under the surface-dense ramp (local terminal speed near the surface is an unstable equilibrium, capping a ballistic climb at ~210 u) — the TASK-25 script uses a sustained scripted vel.y=100/tick climb; do NOT 'simplify' it back to a kick.

BUDGET (45-min iteration): this is all mechanical wiring following existing patterns — no exploration. The unit-testable surface is the pure atmosphere-view.ts (the WebGL path is verified by tsc + the e2e in TASK-28.3, per this repo's convention — see world-manager.test.ts, which only tests the pure buildSystemLayout). Run the FULL `vitest run` (~85 s) once, near the end, not repeatedly.
